business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law foundation under the Panamanian Codes, with Anglo-American commercial and trust law adaptations; unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force 31 October 2012
European Union–Central America Association Agreement, Trade and Investment Pillar, provisionally applied since 1 January 2013
Panama–France Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement, in force 1982
Panama–Netherlands Agreement on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, in force 2001
Panama–Republic of Korea Double Taxation Convention, in force 2021
Panama–Spain Double Taxation Convention, in force 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 29 April 2015 on the Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and WMD Proliferation Financing, as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 74 of 2019 and implemented by Cabinet Decree No. 211 of 2016; Law 129 of 19 December 2020 on the Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Titulares de Beneficiarios) and Executive Decree No. 17 of 9 July 2021; Law 32 of 1927 (as amended by Law 5 of 2011) governing the Sociedad Anónima and the mandatory role of the resident agent; Public Registry tariff regulations of the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential beneficial-owner registry administered by the Dirección Nacional del Registro de Titulares de Beneficiarios under the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias; records are not publicly searchable; access is restricted to competent supervisory authorities, the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), the tax authority (DGI), and obliged entities conducting statutory customer due diligence; bearer-share instruments are immobilized and any certificated forms must be deposited with a licensed custodian)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the origin country is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Consulate of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitutional documents and bylaws of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or equivalent officer of the foreign parent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of valid passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and director (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (banker's opinion) for the substantial shareholder or parent entity
Power of attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent and executing counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (or notarized before a Panamanian notary if signed in Panama)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn corporate due diligence affidavit (declaración jurada) evidencing economic purpose and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding, at any change of ownership or officers, and periodically during the active relationship against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the National List of Terrorists and Proliferators maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), and domestic/international politically exposed person (PEP) databases; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is statutorily required for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and aviation-adjacent trading activities; all screening results, negative news checks, and risk ratings must be documented in the AML/CFT client file per Law 23 of 2015 and Cabinet Decree No. 211 of 2016.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sistema de Trámites en Línea (online module for Certificado de Nombre / name search and reservation: https://oag.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official legal language; proposed corporate names must be written in Latin script; Spanish and English names are uniformly admissible; names in other languages must be accompanied by a Spanish transliteration or translation for registry indexing; the name must include a corporate suffix such as 'S.A.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'Limited'; the name must not be identical or phonetically/visually confusingly similar to any name already registered in the Registro Público de Panamá.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Aviación Civil / Aeronáutica (token requiring prior authorization from the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil de Panamá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant or its resident agent may, within five business days of the administrative notification, file a written reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) with the Dirección General del Registro Público; if the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) before the superior administrative tribunal of the Registro Público; where the rejection is based on a reserved sector token (for example 'Aviación Civil'), the applicant must first obtain the written no-objection clearance from the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil de Panamá and resubmit the application with the clearance and a fresh reservation fee; each resubmission constitutes a new search and expires the contested certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for company registry and official correspondence purposes provided that the licensed resident agent maintains a physical office in Panama where statutory records and corporate books are kept; however, given the 'Distribution of Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus' scope and the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML banking tier, Panamanian banks, the UAF, and the Dirección Nacional del Registro de Titulares de Beneficiarios will require verifiable commercial substance such as a physical operating address, lease agreement, warehouse or inventory contract, and operational records; a purely virtual structure will trigger account refusal and regulatory scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate — quantified at approximately 30% annual probability of a Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) tax inspection and 15% annual probability of an Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) on-site AML inspection for a newly formed aviation-parts trading Sociedad Anónima; unannounced physical inspections by the Registro Público are not standard practice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory — no official filing fee currently prescribed; bundled with resident agent AML compliance services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of parent-entity and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the country of origin / Panamanian consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark plus consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration (RUC) and Aviso de Operación at the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
Municipal commercial license (Aviso de Operación Municipal) for the District of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local municipal ordinance tariff based on declared projected revenue

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary accreditation / import-merchant registration for certified aircraft parts and avionics surplus before the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil (AAC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule of the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 32 of 1927, as amended by Law 5 of 1997 and subsequent reforms (General Law on Corporations), particularly Articles 1 through 123 concerning the incorporation, shares, directors, and corporate formalities of Sociedades Anónimas.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública / Pacto Social (Notarial Deed of Incorporation) registered as the Mercantile Ficha
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Sociedad Anónima; shares may be subscribed and paid in cash or in kind as the Board determines; no escrow account is mandated by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby acknowledges the subscription and issuance of its registered shares to the subscriber named in the minutes, in accordance with Article ___ of the Articles of Incorporation; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at [the address of the Registered Agent], Panama, and the Registered Agent is appointed as agent for service of process; RESOLVED, that the persons named in the minutes are appointed as President, Secretary and Treasurer, with authority to open bank accounts, execute documents and represent the Corporation; and RESOLVED, that officers are authorized to file all statutory registration and municipal license applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name-search and reservation request through the Public Registry's single window, using the proposed Sociedad Anónima name with the corporate suffix 'S.A.' Attach the promoter's due diligence forms and, if applicable, a notarized power of attorney executed before a Panamanian notary. The registry certifies the name reservation for the statutory reservation period.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
Copy of valid passport or national ID of each promoter
Notarized power of attorney (if filed by a representative)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, submit three ranked alternative names; no additional registry fee is charged for the first substitution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Incorporation Deed before Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Coordinate with a licensed Panamanian notary to prepare the Pacto Social and Escritura Pública in Spanish. All incorporators or their attorneys-in-fact must appear, confirm the corporate name, registered office, share capital structure, and initial directors, and execute the deed. The notary will register the deed in the protocol and issue certified testimonio copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft Pacto Social / Articles of Incorporation
Passport copies and proof of identity of directors and officers
Registered agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a formal defect in the draft, amend the articles, re-execute before the same notary, and correct the protocol without new certification fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certified notarial testimonio and the corresponding Formulario de Inscripción at the Mercantile Section. Pay the statutory registration fee calculated on the declared capital. Once approved, the registry creates the Ficha Mercantil and issues a stamped certified copy evidencing the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial testimonio of incorporation deed
Notarized power of attorney for filing (if applicable)
Registry fee payment receipt
Name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an observación or razón, submit corrective articles or clarifications within five business days; if the defect is substantive, a rectification deed may be required before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Corporate Tax ID (RUC) and Tax Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After mercantile registration is complete, file the company pre-registration online via the DGI portal using the corporate Ficha. Designate the legal representative and fiscal domicile. The DGI will issue the permanent RUC number and tax-registration certificate, enabling future import/export activities and domestic invoicing.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of registered incorporation
Copy of the legal representative's Panamanian ID or passport with notarized powers document
Proof of registered office address (utility bill or registered agent letter)
Completed DGI taxpayer registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any mismatched entity data in the DGI portal and attach the certified registry copy; if an observation remains, request an administrative review before the DGI taxpayer services office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Commercial License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Gestión de Ingresos (or relevant municipal revenue office for the district of the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación with the municipality by submitting the RUC, registered incorporation, fire-safety certificate, and proof of address. The municipality assesses the annual commercial license and aviso fee based on declared capital and the line of business (ISIC 4659). This license authorizes the physical or virtual trade of aviation parts.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Registered copy of the incorporation deed
Fire-safety clearance (for any physical storage)
Lease or title evidencing commercial premises, if applicable
Completed municipal Aviso de Operación form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal assessment is questioned, submit the ISIC classification and supporting trade documentation; an internal reconsideration or appeal to the municipal revenue administration may be filed within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección Nacional de Comercio; coordination with the Autoridad Civil de Aeronáutica de Panamá for aviation part traceability, if applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación and Commercial License for wholesale distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, supplemented by MICI import/export registration where goods cross Panamanian borders.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Registrable, low-impact wholesale/warehousing); a formal full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required unless the business adds aircraft disassembly, parts cleaning, or hazardous liquid storage. If expanded to such activities, a full EIA will be mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater is generated in pure trading operations; stormwater runoff from storage facilities must comply with national surface-water quality standards. Any incidental waste, including batteries, hydraulic fluids, or decommissioned parts, must be handled under Resolución AG-0113-2009 and transported only by MiAMBIENTE-licensed handlers. VOC emissions from cleaning or pressure-washing operations, if introduced, must stay below Panamanian ambient air-quality limits and require prior permitting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural/load inspection certificate for warehouse racks and storage areas; occupational health and workplace safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), including an annual risk assessment for manual handling of aviation components.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama; electronic services through the SIRI portal (siri.mef.gob.pa) and the integrated customs platform SIGA/VUPA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Sociedad Anónima must first be registered in the Public Registry of Panama with a resident agent and registered office, and obtain the relevant municipal aviso de operación where required. Thereafter, the company must apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) at the DGI, submitting the public-registry certificate, nominee/legal representative appointment, local fiscal-domicile evidence, powers of attorney for the responsible representative, and passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owners/directors. RUC serves for both income tax and ITBMS/VAT identification. Foreign entities without a Panamanian fixed establishment may still be registered for specific withholding and export-zero-rating obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope; the Sociedad Anónima is a per-se corporation, not pass-through, and Panamanian tax is imposed on Panama-source income only. Foreign-source income, including offshore aviation-parts trading where title passes outside Panama and no Panama fixed establishment is involved, generally falls outside the taxable base.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch entity election is available in Panama. Entity classification follows the legal form of the Sociedad Anónima. Limited elections exist for special regimes such as free-trade-zone (Zona Franca) licensing or the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime, and an eligible small taxpayer may elect simplified income tax treatment, but an S.A. remains a corporate taxpayer for ITBMS purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y la Prestación de Servicios) — Panama's national VAT-like transfer tax on the sale of tangible movable property and services rendered for consideration in Panama.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0.00 — no turnover de minimis applies to a Panamanian S.A. engaged in commercial transfers or imports; ITBMS registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply or import. Natural-person small taxpayers may use a simplified fixed-payment regime, but this does not alter mandatory registration for a corporate entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing for active taxpayers. Invoices must be issued as Documento Tributario Electrónico (DTE) XML through the DGI's free e-invoice portal or an authorized PSFE service provider. The DGI SIRI system performs near-real-time validation and issues a fiscal authorization code; digital stamping is represented by the DGI validation code and QR. Export zero-rated invoices, customs export declarations, and supporting transport documents must be cross-matched through SIGA/VUPA at the time of shipment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% ITBMS rate is available for (i) goods physically exported from Panama to a foreign buyer, (ii) services rendered entirely outside Panama or services supplied for direct use abroad, and (iii) sales to duty-free zones and supplies for international maritime/aircraft operations, including commercial aircraft rotables and surplus parts destined for foreign airlines or international carriers. Eligibility requires the seller to be a registered ITBMS taxpayer, customs export formalities to be completed in the taxpayer's name, and the goods to leave Panamanian territory within the period stated in the export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted in SIGA/VUPA
Certificate of Export / exit validation issued by the Customs Authority
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT credit advice, or bank payment evidence in the seller's name
ITBMS zero-rated invoice including the export legend and DGI electronic authorization
Acquisition/Title documentation evidencing the aircraft parts and export value where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and the Customs Authority may audit export files and cross-check the customs declaration, transport documents, and banking remittance. If zero-rating is claimed without proven physical export, with false values, or where goods are re-introduced into Panamanian commerce, the entire ITBMS is clawed back at 7% plus statutory late-payment recargos. The Código Fiscal and Customs Law 112 of 2017 impose omitted-tax surcharges, fines of up to B/. 50,000 or more for false customs declarations, potential criminal liability for customs evasion/contraband, publication of tax defaulters, and the temporary suspension or cancellation of the RUC for repeat offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama maintains no statutory central bank; the U.S. dollar circulates as legal tender under the Monetary Agreement with the United States. Banking supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), while Banco Nacional de Panamá carries out fiscal-agency and clearing-house functions. No foreign exchange administration exists because the monetary standard is full dollarization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian balboa (PAB) is a fractional denomination of the U.S. dollar at a fixed 1:1 rate, creating a fully convertible, unified currency zone. There are no controls on current or capital account transactions, no exchange-rate bands, and no government approval for inward or outward remittances. Profit remittances, dividends, royalties, loan repayments, and capital repatriation are unrestricted. Panama applies territorial taxation; non-Panamanian source income is outside the domestic tax net, and foreign shareholders may repatriate Panamanian-source profits after the 10% dividend withholding tax (subject to double-tax-treaty relief, if applicable). No pre-clearance or exchange-control permit is required for any cross-border capital movement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to surrender foreign currency. A Panamanian exporter may retain 100% of export receipts in any freely convertible currency at any bank, local or offshore. Export earnings may remain offshore indefinitely, provided the territorial tax return accurately identifies Panamanian-source revenue and correctly excludes offshore receipts from taxable income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (state fiscal-agent settlement and collection)
Operational Account (trade settlement and SWIFT MT103)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Low-to-Medium. Panama has no bespoke e-money institution (EMI) licensing regime analogous to the EU; fintech activities generally require a banking license, a 'Sociedad Financiera' license, or Sandbox authorisation from the SBP. Nonresident offshore EMIs (for example, Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) may be used for liquidity pooling and cross-border collections without a Panamanian license, but local banks will typically reject remittance counterparties that cannot provide complete KYC and beneficial-owner data. Key constraints: (i) EMIs are not recognised as banking counterparties eligible for custody of aircraft-escrow proceeds under SBP guidance; (ii) any EMI receiving funds from a Panamanian account must furnish an AML/CFT compliance statement and UBO disclosure; (iii) the SBP's transaction reporting threshold (USD 10,000 equivalent under Law 23 of 2015) applies equally to bank and EMI channels. The recommended approach is dual-rail: maintain a licensed Panama bank account for settlement and use an FATF-equivalent supervised EMI only for low-value payouts, with the EMI added as a sub-account at the Panamanian bank after prior approval of the compliance officer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a standard Panamanian S.A. used in aviation-parts trading, physical presence is normally required. Bank KYC policies implementing SBP Agreement 1-2014 mandate in-person identification for each director, each shareholder holding 10% or more, and the senior compliance officer. Remote opening is permitted only if the principals appear before a Panamanian notary or a Panamanian consulate, all corporate documents are apostilled, and a local attorney-in-fact is appointed. At least one beneficial owner or managing director must attend a bank interview in Panama City; the bank's Compliance Officer may waive this only for a publicly listed parent company under FATF-equivalent supervision.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee-shareholder heritage or a historical bearer-share structure that creates opacity in the beneficial-ownership trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registro Público certificate of the S.A. 'carpeta' and incorporation registration; sworn declaration of ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) under Law 23 of 2015; issued entry from the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) showing current tax ID and beneficial owners; notarized chain of powers of attorney; corporate resolution confirming that no bearer shares are outstanding; passport copies and two bank reference letters for each UBO; certified Spanish or English translations of all source documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade in certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics that may trigger dual-use, export-control, or sanctions-screening queries, especially if parts could be diverted to military or OFAC-designated carriers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FAA / EASA airworthiness certificates and Certificates of Conformance; manufacturer's traceability sheets (Boeing, Airbus, IAI, Safran, Pratt & Whitney); BIS / EAR classification certificate for ECCN 9A991 or 7A994 (as applicable); end-user attestation and red-flag screening report from OFAC SDN / consolidated screening systems; commercial invoices and packing lists showing exact harmonized-tariff classification; insurance certificates and customs clearance records for each shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or high-value wire transfers immediately after account opening that are inconsistent with the company's projected turnover, or an invoicing and delivery jurisdiction mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the last two years, or an opening balance sheet plus 12-month projection; board resolution specifying authorised signatories and wire dollar limits; purchase orders, sales contracts, and proforma invoices reflecting documented OEM or surplus-parts pricing; freight-forwarder delivery confirmation (airway bill, bill of lading) for each shipment; comprehensive source-of-wealth memorandum for all inbound injections above USD 25,000; documentary evidence of the underlying aviation transaction appended to every wire instruction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from foreign shareholders must be routed by SWIFT MT103 with the remitter's true name, a source-of-funds statement, and field 70 specifying 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / PAID-IN CAPITAL'. Funds must be credited to the Panama S.A.'s USD operational account at a licensed bank. No pre-registration, central-bank approval, or exchange-control licence is required. Retain the following compliance file: (i) board or shareholder resolution approving the capital injection; (ii) shareholder registry update; (iii) bank-issued credit notification; (iv) UBO declarations when the injection originates from a trust or treasury entity. If the single injection exceeds USD 1,000,000, expect enhanced due diligence requiring a comprehensive source-of-wealth summary and audited financial statements of the remitting parent or beneficial owner. For maximum clearing efficiency, use the bank's primary U.S. correspondent and include the beneficiary's full BIC/PPS details.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments and refunds for surplus commercial aircraft parts should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct payments, or via an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) issued by a Panama bank for large procurement orders. Recommended hierarchy: (a) direct SWIFT MT103 to reputable OEM and FAA/EASA repair stations up to USD 250,000; (b) confirmed irrevocable LC at sight for purchases above USD 250,000; (c) documentary collection (D/A or D/P) for intra-Latin American exchanges; (d) discounting under LC through the relationship bank's trade desk when supply-chain financing is required. All outbound instructions must include the trade reference, ISIC 4659 description, and applicable BIS export classification, and must pass OFAC / CMIC sanctions screening. For dollar-clearing, prefer Fedwire or CHIPS if the receiving bank is a U.S. correspondent; otherwise, MT103 is mandatory for commercial trade — never use MT202 COV for consumer or vendor payments unless specifically mandated by the receiving bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot outright transactions against USD (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) with T+2 settlement
Vanilla FX forward contracts up to twelve months for EUR, CHF, and Asian trade-flow currencies
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term EUR/USD exposure on aviation-finance leases
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for low-liquidity exotic currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) with investment-grade international banking counterparties
Currency options and zero-premium collar structures for hedged transactions, subject to SBP suitability and internal treasury policy approvals

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax – Tasa Única (flat USD 300 franchise fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, through the licensed Panamanian resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March each year for every Panama S.A., irrespective of taxable activity or income level
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory surcharge and interest are assessed on late payment; failure to pay the annual corporation tax for three consecutive years exposes the S.A. to administrative dissolution and strike-off by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Declaration – Formulario 103 (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; by 31 March for a calendar-year S.A. This is required only where the corporation realizes Panamanian-source income or maintains local taxable activity; a purely offshore S.A. has no nil-return filing obligation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment surcharge of 5% per month or fraction thereof on the tax due, up to a maximum of 50%, plus statutory interest; persistent nonfiling may generate tax liens and involuntary dissolution risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Registry Update – Declaración de Beneficiario Final
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry through the resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; the resident agent must also obtain an annual UBO re-confirmation when the March Tasa Única is paid.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to USD 50,000 for nonfiling, material inaccuracies, or false beneficial ownership information; prolonged noncompliance may lead to resident-agent resignation and loss of registered status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit by a Panamanian certified public accountant is mandatory when the S.A. exceeds the accounting and audit thresholds set by Law 52 of 2016 and DGI regulations, generally annual gross revenue above USD 3 million or total assets above USD 5 million; an exempt offshore trading S.A. below these thresholds is not required to file audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS / NIIF as adopted in Panama; small and medium entities may apply NIIF para PYMES (IFRS for SMEs). Statutory books must be kept in Spanish or bilingual form and remain available for DGI inspection.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each share transfer must be recorded promptly in the register of shareholders, and the resident agent must update the DGI beneficial ownership declaration within 30 calendar days of the transaction. As part of the annual maintenance cycle, the resident agent secures a written confirmation from the directors and beneficial owners of the current UBO schedule before the March Tasa Única payment; no duplicate UBO filing is required if the DGI record is already accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders and share transfers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,000 per engagement if the mandatory audit threshold is triggered; no audit cost for a purely offshore exempt S.A.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama operates a territorial income tax system. The standard 25% corporate income tax applies only to income derived from Panamanian sources. Extraterritorial trading income earned by a Sociedad Anónima from sales of surplus commercial aircraft parts to foreign airlines, when all relevant contracting, delivery, and payment activities occur outside Panama, is outside the ISR tax base and therefore bears an effective income tax rate of 0%. No general statutory tax holiday is in force, but certain targeted regimes (e.g., Multinational Headquarters Law 41 of 2007 at a preferential 10%, and special maritime/aircraft lease incentives) require qualifying local substance. There are no statutory deductions for foreign-source costs or losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 200 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta – Personas Jurídicas), filed electronically through the DGI ‘Declaraciones Web’ portal (https://declaracionesweb.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the last day of the third calendar month following the close of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer the deadline is March 31. A different fiscal year-end may apply upon prior DGI authorization, with the return due three months after that fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), legal name of the Sociedad Anónima, fiscal year end, ISIC code, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Panama RUC issued at incorporation. For a completely offshore trading entity, still complete this field using the registered agent's address as the fiscal domicile; there is no requirement to have a local operating office for this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian sources, including sales made within Panama, services performed in Panama, or use of assets located in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For surplus aircraft parts distribution conducted entirely abroad, enter zero. Only sales physically executed or completed within Panama should be reported in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from exports, foreign trade, and services performed or goods sold outside Panama. Reported for informational purposes but excluded from the taxable ISR base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all sales to foreign airlines, MROs, and trading partners in this line. Include full documentary support, such as contracts, bills of lading, and banking routing records demonstrating foreign-source character.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses strictly attributable to Panamanian-source income. Foreign-source costs and general administrative expenses not allocable to Panama-source income are not deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panamanian-source income exists, enter zero. Do not deduct offshore purchasing costs, transportation, or foreign warehouse expenses against extraterritorial revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or loss calculated as Panamanian-source gross income minus deductible Panamanian-source expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an extraterritorial-only operation, this line is zero. Foreign trading losses are not recognised and cannot be carried forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax determined at the statutory 25% rate applied to Line 550.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero when no Panamanian-source taxable income is reported. Any advance tax payments already made will still be credited in the corresponding credit fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, withholding tax credits, and tax prepayments applicable to the ISR liability for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may only credit Panamanian tax actually paid or withheld on Panamanian-source income. Foreign tax credits are not available for Panama ISR purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 800 – Saldo de deuda o a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between the ISR determined and the sum of credits and prepayments. Positive is a tax due; negative is a refundable balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an entity with no Panamanian-source income, this line will be zero. If paid advance assessments exceeded the zero liability, the excess is refundable as a preference but subject to DGI audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment triggers a monthly surcharge of 1% of the tax amount due, capped at 20% of such tax amount, plus interest at the DGI statutory rate. Administrative fines for failure to file range from B/.100 to B/.5,000. Repeated non-filing may result in an official estimated assessment and criminal tax evasion prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10.00% on any dividend or profit distribution made by a Panamanian corporation out of Panamanian-source taxable income. Dividends paid out of extraterritorial income are not subject to this statutory dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement, the shareholder or recipient of Panama-source investment income must file an application with the DGI for a Certificado de Residencia Fiscal (TRC), attaching the corporate registration certificate, governing documents, and a declaration of tax-residency. The TRC is then delivered to the source-country paying entity before the payment date. The payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source and requires a beneficial ownership declaration and, where necessary, supporting financial statements. Panama's DTA network is limited but includes agreements with Mexico, Chile, Spain, France, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Singapore, UK, and UAE, generally following the OECD Model.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panama WHT for payment to non-residents of royalties for intangibles used in Panama is 25.00%; statutory WHT on interest earned on Panamanian-source loans or credit obligations is 10.00%. Under applicable DTAs, royalty rates may be reduced to 5.00%-15.00% and interest to 0.00%-10.00%, subject to submission of a valid TRC and beneficial ownership confirmation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Panama Transfer Pricing regime (Law 8 of 2010 and Decree 28 of 2012) requires preparation of a Local File and, where applicable, a Master File when the aggregate value of related-party transactions entered into by the Panamanian taxpayer equals or exceeds B/.1,000,000.00 (US$1,000,000, as the Balboa is pegged to the US dollar). A Master File is also required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenues exceed B/.300,000,000.00. For taxpayers not meeting these thresholds, a simplified Declaration of Transactions with Related Parties is still required annually.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Ley 254 of 2020) and implementing rules impose reporting and substance requirements on tax-resident entities carrying on 'relevant activities', which include distribution and service centres. For a surplus commercial aircraft parts distributor that is tax-resident in Panama, at least one local director, physical premises in Panama, or adequate local employees and expenditure proportionate to the profits must be maintained and reported annually via the ‘Aviso de Sustancia Económica’. If the Sociedad Anónima is managed from abroad, compensates its directors outside Panama, and has no Panamanian-source operating activity, it is considered a non-resident for ESR purposes and has no filing obligation. However, claiming tax-residency under a DTA while lacking economic substance will trigger ESR penalties and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Panamanian-source revenues from Form 200, fabricating deductions, or concealing foreign bank accounts and sales proceeds derived from Panamanian commercial activity in order to reduce the 25% ISR or the 10% dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under Article 216-A of the Penal Code is punishable with imprisonment of three to five years and a fine equal to two to four times the amount of tax evaded. The DGI may also impose administrative surcharges of up to 20% plus interest on the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or direct treasury routing schemes are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax debt. The DGI may apply civil seizure against personal assets, and a criminal conviction can result in a travel ban and disqualification from holding office in Panamanian companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Panama S.A. as a pure incorporation with no local decision making, no physical office, no Panamanian employees, and no economic activity, while nonetheless claiming to be a Panama tax resident to secure DTA benefits or shield foreign trades from substance scrutiny.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to meet Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2020) results in fines of up to B/.100,000 for inadequate substance, separate fines for failure to file the annual substance notice, and, in severe or repeat cases, cancellation of the company's registration and denial of the certificate of tax residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the appointed resident agent are personally liable for false declarations of substance. Penalties include personal fines, suspension or permanent revocation of the resident agent license, and criminal sanctions for signing fraudulent statements. A director who is removed may also be barred from entering Panama pending tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML – Money Laundering and Unregulated Payment Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing aircraft parts transactions through nominee bank accounts, failing to maintain and disclose a beneficial ownership register to the Superintendencia de Bancos/FinCEN-equivalent, engaging in cash structuring for purchases of surplus inventory, or wilfully concealing high-risk counterparties in violation of the AML 'know-your-customer' obligations under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 and the Penal Code, money laundering offences carry imprisonment of five to ten years, asset forfeiture, and fines of up to B/.1,000,000. Administrative AML fines for non-reporting subjects reach B/.500,000.00 per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and any beneficial owner who knowingly uses shell entities or nominee vehicles for laundering or sanctions evasion face criminal prosecution, travel bans, extradition eligibility, and civil liability up to the full value of assets laundered. Individual directors may also be disqualified from management of any Panamanian regulated entity.
